components.name: Tooltip
components.description: Component wrapper for tooltip display triggered on hover or focus.

props.name: children
props.description: Trigger element(s) that activate the tooltip.

props.name: anchorRef
props.description: External anchor ref for sibling mode.

props.name: content
props.description: Tooltip content, typically short text.

props.name: placement
props.description: Position relative to the anchor element. Logical: start/end resolve against the popover's own inherited direction (RTL mirrors in pure CSS).

props.name: alignment
props.description: Alignment along the placement axis. Logical: start/end resolve against the popover's own inherited direction (RTL mirrors in pure CSS).

props.name: delay
props.description: Show delay in milliseconds.

props.name: hideDelay
props.description: Hide delay in milliseconds.

props.name: focusTrigger
props.description: Controls when focus events trigger the tooltip.

props.name: touchTrigger
props.description: What a tap does where there is no hover. auto opens on tap unless the trigger performs an action of its own (a button, link, or form control), whose tap belongs to the control. tap always opens; use it for an info icon rendered as a button, whose only job is to reveal the tooltip. none never opens on touch.

props.name: isEnabled
props.description: Enables or disables the tooltip triggers.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.description: Callback fired when tooltip visibility changes. Called with true when shown and false when hidden.

props.name: hasHoverIndication
props.description: Shows a dashed underline on the trigger element.

props.name: isDefaultOpen
props.description: Whether the tooltip should be shown on mount. Still dismissible.

props.name: isOpen
props.description: Controlled open state for the tooltip.

anatomy.name: Tooltip surface
anatomy.description: Painted overlay surface that presents the tooltip.

anatomy.name: Tooltip text
anatomy.description: Tooltip content rendered within the surface.

usage.description: A short text hint that appears on hover or focus, anchored to a trigger element. Use it to describe icon-only buttons, show the full text of truncated labels, or provide supplementary context without cluttering the UI.

bestPractices.description: Keep tooltip content concise: aim for under 140 characters of plain text.
Add a tooltip to icon-only buttons and controls that lack a visible label.
Set touchTrigger to tap when the trigger is a button whose only job is revealing the tooltip, such as an info icon: touch has no hover, and auto keeps the tap for triggers that perform an action.
Place interactive elements like links or buttons inside a tooltip; use HoverCard or Popover instead.
Use tooltips for essential information that users must see to complete a task.

en.name: TopNav
en.description: Main navigation bar container with slot-based layout. Children are accepted as an alias for startContent.

props.name: heading
props.description: Heading slot content (logo, brand): positioned at the left edge of the nav bar.

props.name: startContent
props.description: Start content slot for navigation items or breadcrumbs: positioned after the heading, left-aligned.

props.name: children
props.description: Alias for startContent. Prefer startContent when composing with heading, centerContent, or endContent; children keeps the common React nav-item pattern from silently dropping items.

props.name: centerContent
props.description: Center content slot (tabs, search bar, primary navigation): when provided, switches the layout to a three-column CSS grid for true horizontal centering.

props.name: endContent
props.description: End content slot for search, icons, or user profile: positioned at the right edge.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible label for the navigation landmark, applied as aria-label on the <nav> element.

props.name: xstyle
props.description: StyleX styles for layout customization (margins, positioning, sizing). Must be a stylex.create() value: not an inline style object like style={{}}.

usage.description: TopNav is a horizontal navigation bar for product-level navigation in application headers. Use TopNav for 5 or fewer always-visible navigation items, or minimal navigation paired with search and controls. For complex navigation hierarchies, use a sidebar; to filter content, use tabs or filter buttons instead.

bestPractices.description: Include a product logo and name in the heading slot to clearly identify the application.
Limit primary navigation items to 5 or fewer for quick scanning and minimal cognitive load.
Avoid using TopNav to filter page content; use Tabs or filter controls instead.
Avoid deeply nested navigation hierarchies; keep menus to one level of depth.

anatomy.name: Product icon and name
anatomy.description: Identifies the product in the navigation bar.

anatomy.name: Navigation items
anatomy.description: Primary links for product-level destinations.

anatomy.name: More menu
anatomy.description: Overflow menu for additional navigation items.

anatomy.name: Flex area
anatomy.description: Flexible region for search, primary action buttons, or other controls.

usage.description: An expandable tree structure for displaying hierarchical data with branch connector lines. Use it for file explorers, nested category browsers, or any interface that visualizes parent-child relationships.

bestPractices.description: Provide meaningful labels and icons for each node to make the hierarchy easy to scan.
Pre-expand important branches so users see key content immediately.

Leaf rows reserve space for a chevron column whenever the tree has any expandable item to line up under; only a fully flat tree (no expandable items at all) renders its rows flush. Rely on this rather than nudging indentation with custom CSS.
Nest more than 4–5 levels deep; flatten the structure or use a different pattern.
Use a tree for flat, non-hierarchical data; use a List instead.

usage.description: An expandable tree structure for displaying hierarchical data with branch connector lines. Use it for file explorers, nested category browsers, or any interface that visualizes parent-child relationships.

bestPractices.description: Provide meaningful labels and icons for each node to make the hierarchy easy to scan.
Pre-expand important branches so users see key content immediately.

Leaf rows reserve space for a chevron column whenever the tree has any expandable item to line up under; only a fully flat tree (no expandable items at all) renders its rows flush. Rely on this rather than nudging indentation with custom CSS.
Nest more than 4–5 levels deep; flatten the structure or use a different pattern.
Use a tree for flat, non-hierarchical data; use a List instead.

usage.description: Renders content in the accessibility tree while hiding it visually. Use for accessible names on icon-only controls, aria-live announcement regions, and supplementary screen-reader context. Deliberately has no styling props; the whole point is to stay invisible.

bestPractices.description: Use to give icon-only buttons and controls an accessible name that screen readers announce.
Render as a block element (as="div") with aria-live to announce dynamic updates like drag-and-drop or result counts.
Use it to hide content from everyone; it stays in the accessibility tree; use conditional rendering or `hidden` to remove content entirely.
Put interactive controls inside it; the content is not visible and cannot receive pointer input.
